Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first establish the workspace contract from `README.md`, then inspect the inherited rollout evidence and both required control skills before proposing or editing the single candidate. I’ll keep all changes confined to this Phase 2 workspace.

I’m now using the required `fish-control-primitives` shelf to constrain mechanism transfer, and the `read-wake-visual-signals-first` skill because this policy must be grounded in both moving-window visual views. I’ll use those instructions to shape the evidence review; adopting a bookshelf primitive will depend on what the inherited rollouts actually show.

The inherited population is a narrow set of successful captures, not a clean success-versus-crash split. I’ll therefore compare the strongest aggregate-distance capture against the most informative weaker capture/terminal-motion variant, while also checking the replicated pair and the assigned parent’s optimizer notes. This preserves the skill’s intent without inventing a failure class that is not present.

The visual requirement is satisfied: all four combined sheets show self-propelled motion, a coherent alternating top-down vortex street, matching three-dimensional Lambda2 structures, and the same smooth capture arc; there is no prewarm artifact or instability. The strongest route-handoff pair is visually indistinguishable from the weaker full-observer and late-handoff samples, so the remaining decision has to come from phase-resolved trajectory, load, and actuator histories rather than wake appearance alone.

The evidence isolates a new actuator-coordinate test. In the best handoff rollout, every terminal moment above `0.012` occurs during near-common two-joint acceleration; the 29 such samples average `0.01260` moment while retaining strong radial progress, and the peak (`0.014319` at `1.217L`) has commands `(-30.72,-27.63)`—almost pure summed/tail-tangent acceleration. By contrast, peak yaw and cross-track motion occur under opposite-sign commands. I’ll preserve the best route handoff and introduce only a bounded, terminal, high-common-command projection, leaving the differential command and ordinary carrier strokes unchanged. This directly tests peak-load relief without another steering gain or fast observation gate.

The bookshelf influenced this edit at the mechanism level: it supports separating posterior reactive/tail-tangent loading from the inter-joint traveling-wave coordinate, while the rollout—not any published gain—sets where the projection activates. I’m recording that transfer and its falsification boundary in the required notes before touching the policy.

Both required provenance files are now materially updated. The candidate keeps the strongest sampled broad route handoff and adds only the new terminal common-coordinate projector; the durable guidance now records the evaluated failure of progress-qualified route arbitration, so later workers won’t mistake its tiny yaw/load changes for improvement. I’m checking that the actual policy diff contains no accidental controller changes and then running the mandated non-CFD contract checks.

The policy diff is clean: relative to the evaluated best handoff, only two owned parameters and the final common/differential projection were added. The guidance wrapper hit the same rendered-workspace defect documented by the parent—`README.md` repeats the identical prefill marker twice—so I won’t mutate the read-only root contract to hide it. I’ll run its semantic comparison against the unique assigned parent directly, along with the boundary and schema guards, and will still invoke the configured check-runner as required.

The local non-CFD checks pass: solver boundary, unique-parent guidance semantics, one public definition per function, and parameter schema (`75` declared fields, `73` referenced, none missing). Julia is not installed, so the executable smoke is unavailable. I’m now invoking the workspace’s configured check-runner, as mandated; it should independently report the same rendered-marker limitation and run every check its environment supports.

The configured checker itself cannot start because its pinned `gpt-5.4-mini` model is unsupported by this ChatGPT account; it failed before reading the workspace. That is an environment/configuration blocker, not a policy failure. I’ve already run the same checks locally and will finish with an offline command-coordinate audit plus a final content review; no CFD will be run.

The offline projector audit is consistent with the intended scope: it changes no command before `3L`, activates on `101/601` terminal samples, preserves the differential command to floating-point precision, and applies `10.4%` common relief at the recorded peak-load event (maximum realized relief `16.2%`). I’ve documented these as a non-dynamic audit—not as CFD evidence—and am doing the final pass over the completed files now.

Implemented exactly one candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:603) preserves the best route handoff and adds bounded terminal common-acceleration relief.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1) contains the visual diagnosis, evidence, bookshelf transfer, hypothesis, and falsification criteria.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:218) records the negative result for progress-qualified route arbitration.

Boundary and schema checks pass: 75 declared parameters, 73 referenced, none missing. The configured checker could not launch because its pinned model is unavailable; Julia is also absent. The equivalent static checks passed. No CFD was run.
